claim: In February 2019, Concert — a "public-benefit company" created by Israel's Ministry of Strategic Affairs (originally named Kela Shlomo, "Solomon's Sling") to channel grants to advocacy groups — awarded nearly $1.3 million to Christians United for Israel, the largest pro-Israel group in America. Leaked documents reported by The Forward in 2020 showed U.S. pro-Israel groups failing to disclose Israeli government grants; none registered as foreign agents. CUFI's parent entity, the CUFI Church Association, is designated a church by the IRS, so it files no public financial reports. A 2026 Global Project Against Hate and Extremism report states CUFI has accepted direct funding from the Israeli government.

sources.label: The Forward — Aiden Pink, "U.S. pro-Israel groups failed to disclose grants from Israeli government" (Aug 31, 2020).
sources.quote: Christians United for Israel, the largest pro-Israel group in America, which was awarded nearly $1.3 million in February 2019 for 10 week-long pilgrimages to the Holy Land

notes: From @breakfromrealitytv reel DZC6powxFYt (part 4 of its CUFI series). The reel cites GPAHE 'published April 7th, 2026' — correct — and attributes the nondisclosure reporting to The Forward; the caption dates it 2022 but the Pink article is Aug 31, 2020. The Forward piece names the recipients of Concert money: CUFI ($1.3M, Feb 2019), Israel Allies Foundation (>$100k, 2019), Hasbara Fellowships (>$1M), StandWithUs, America-Israel Friendship League; the Ministry of Strategic Affairs pledged to match private donations to Concert up to $37.5M over four years.
